$comment: FR-148. Every bundle under fixtures/manifests/bundles/ that the product does NOT accept
must appear here with the reason it must be rejected and the diagnostic it is rejected by.
Enforced by core/src/fixture_corpus_tests.rs, which runs inside the existing `Rust test` CI job.
Base: a fresh default project — one `default` workspace, no agents, no workflows
into the current config before building it, so validity is never a property of the file
alone; against the fully seeded harness five bundles are rejected for the scaffolding's
own `basic` workflow instead of their own contents.
`expect` is a list because a bundle holding several retired constructs is rejected on
whichever the merge reaches first, and the merge walks a HashMap. Every alternative is
spelled out per workflow — the list is an enumeration, not a wildcard.
`rotted_count` is compared for equality, not as a ceiling: retiring rot has to move this
number down, and it did. FR-148 froze 19 rotted entries; FR-149 deleted all 19 bundles
and their entries, so the count is 0. It stays a declared number rather than being
dropped, because 0 is a claim — a bundle that rots tomorrow has to move it back up,
and a ceiling of 0 would read the same while accepting the first regression silently.

expect: env fromRef 'claude-opus' references unknown store
env fromRef 'minimax' references unknown store
bundles.reason: `claude-opus` comes from docs/workflow/claude-secret.yaml, but `minimax` comes from docs/workflow/minimax-secret.yaml, which is gitignored (.gitignore:13) — a developer's local secrets file. This manifest therefore can never be accepted from the index alone, and that is not a defect to fix: the alternative is committing a secrets file. Environment rather than dependent because the missing half is not in the repository at all. Either alternative may fire first; the merge order is not stable.

expect: unknown variant `store_put`
bundles.reason: Deliberately mixed, like coordination-strangler-parity: the `-legacy` workflows hold the pre-migration shape of the two production store_inputs consumers plus one isolated case per other retired kind, and the `-migrated` ones hold the shape that must still apply. test-pipeline-variable-retirement.sh splits it and runs each half. The `-legacy` half is also the rollback evidence for FR-156, kept so the removal stays reversible. The gate that applied it, test-pipeline-variable-retirement.sh, was retired on 2026-08-16; the bundle stays because core's every_tracked_bundle_is_accepted_or_declared derives its corpus from git ls-files and so still asserts that each declared diagnostic fires — a cheaper and less enumerated check than the gate it outlived. FR-173 retired the named codes at the v0.7 window; the bundle is still refused, now by serde through deny_unknown_fields rather than by a [legacy_*] diagnostic. The declaration records what the product actually says, which is why it had to be re-observed rather than rewritten from the old wording.
